title: Container Instances: a container with no orchestrator

videos.script: Lessons 1 to 6 gave you machines. You picked a size and an image, and you paid for the machine whether the shop was busy or not. {{group}} Container Instances takes the machine away. You hand Azure an image, a size and a restart policy, and it runs your container. There is no cluster to look after and no node to patch. What you get is a container group: one or more containers on one host, sharing a network and a lifecycle. {{shop}} This lesson also builds the shop. A small Python service with four pages, in an image of its own. You will run it with Docker, call it, and read its log. The same image comes back in Container Apps, in AKS and in App Service. {{yaml}} Then you will write it down for Azure, twice. Once as the YAML file the command line takes, and once in Bicep, which the compiler checks. {{restart}} Next come sizes and restart policies. A server should come back when it dies. A nightly report that finished should stay finished. {{gaps}} Last, what Container Instances is for, and what it leaves out. It has no scaling, no rolling update and no load balancer. Knowing that is how you know when to use something else.
